title: [D8 Guardrails] Architectural boundary tests over dependencies and stores
summary: `concept/06-technology.md`'s five rejection rows — graph framework, higher-level agent frameworks, workflow engine, hosted tracing, and the second store (relational profile / vector / checkpoint) — are now executable in `tests/test_architecture_boundary.py`: eleven tests covering what the existing boundary tests did not reach, plus two meta-tests that re-parse the technology table on every run so adding or reversing a rejection is red until a test carries it. `docs/decisions/0039-architectural-boundaries.md` is the record a reversal has to go through, and a test requires it to exist and to name every rejection it governs. Nothing in `src/` changed; the increment adds no capability, it makes five existing commitments fail loudly instead of quietly.
assumption_validated: That the rejections had real holes rather than being already covered by the dependency boundary — and they did, six of them. Measured, not argued: (1) `tests/test_dependency_boundary.py` allows every name in `sys.stdlib_module_names`, which it must, so `import sqlite3` passed it by construction and a checkpoint store needs no dependency at all; (2) the second-store clients were never enumerated anywhere, only `sqlalchemy` as one entry in a list about the model client; (3) graph frameworks, agent frameworks and workflow engines had no table; (4) nothing checked the filesystem, and `concept/03-architecture.md` names file-backed agent memory as the convenient default a framework brings; (5) nothing checked the engine's own catalogue, where a `CREATE SINK ... WITH (connector = 'kafka', ...)` is an egress channel with its own credentials that no import scan sees; (6) `tests/test_broker.py` looks for `confluent_kafka` by name inside `helena/broker.py`, so `aiokafka` imported by any other module passed all of it. Each of the seven structural gates was then proved to bite by inducing its failure and reverting — see the verification detail.
makes_buildable: Task 51 (secrets hygiene) inherits two things it would otherwise build: the `_installed()` helper, which answers 'does this resolve in this environment at all' rather than 'is it declared', and the finding that a package declared-but-not-locked still gets installed by `uv run` (see failed_approaches) — which is the mechanism by which a credential-bearing SDK could arrive without a lockfile entry. Task 55 (deferred register and open questions) gets `REJECTIONS` as a live index from a concept-note row to the test that holds it, the same shape as task 49's `COVERED_BY`, and it already carries the two provisional entries that register needs: 'Higher-level agent frameworks | Deferred' and the model-client escalation in docs/decisions/0020 §1. Any later task that adds a persistence target now has one place that says so out loud — the engine catalogue query and `test_the_only_external_clients_are_the_engine_driver_and_the_kafka_client` both fail on a new one, naming the rule rather than the symptom.

verification.detail: 1793 passed in 661 s against the final tree. The new module is 11 tests, 10 of which need nothing running; `uv run pytest -q tests/test_architecture_boundary.py` is 11 passed in 28 s. `uv lock --check` resolves 17 packages unchanged and `uv run python -m compileall -q src tests scripts` is clean. The pre-change baseline recorded by task 49 was 1781 passed, 1 skipped; the skip was the pinned-binaries one, which passes here because both binaries were answering. SEVEN GATE MUTATIONS WERE INDUCED, OBSERVED RED, AND REVERTED, with `git status` clean after each: (1) `import sqlite3` added to src/helena/status.py -> test_no_stdlib_store_module_is_imported_by_the_package red; (2) `import tempfile`, a `.write_text()` and an `open(path, "a")` added to the same module -> test_the_package_writes_to_no_file_and_starts_no_process red, naming all three; (3) a `| Feature store | **Rejected** |` row appended to concept/06-technology.md -> test_every_rejection_in_the_technology_table_has_a_test_here red; (4) 'Workflow engine | **Rejected**' changed to '**Adopted**' in the same note -> test_the_technology_table_still_records_each_rejection red on the diff; (5) `redis` and `langgraph` added to pyproject.toml's dependencies -> the second-store and framework tests red, each naming the decision record; (6) a test named in REJECTIONS renamed -> the meta-test red on the unresolved name; (7) the decision record deleted, then present but no longer naming 'Workflow engine' -> test_reversing_a_rejection_requires_a_decision_record red in both forms. The engine-side test was also proved to catch what it is for rather than assumed to: a throwaway schema with one `CREATE SOURCE ... WITH (connector = 'datagen', ...)` returns `rw_sources [('probe_source',)]` from the same schema-scoped statement that returns empty for the migrated schema. Measured against the pinned RisingWave 3.0.3 on 2026-09-12: rw_sources, rw_sinks, rw_connections and rw_secrets are all empty for the migrated schema and cluster-wide.

deferred: Step 4 of the task — 'no component codes against a broker-specific API beyond the Kafka protocol' — was already implemented, by task 3, and was deliberately not re-implemented. `tests/test_broker.py` asserts that only `helena/broker.py` imports a Kafka client, that it binds only the eight approved wire-protocol names, that it reaches the network no other way (so blink's REST port on 30004 is unreachable), and that no module in the package holds an address-shaped literal. Duplicating any of that would give one property two definitions that can disagree. What was added is the half that module structurally cannot see: it looks for `confluent_kafka` by name inside one file, so a SECOND client (`kafka-python`, `aiokafka`, `quixstreams`) or a vendor SDK imported by some other module passed every one of its assertions, as does an `rpk` subprocess. `test_no_broker_specific_client_is_declared_imported_or_installed` and the `subprocess` entry in the filesystem scan close those two.

The hosted-tracing declaration and environment checks were likewise not duplicated. `tests/test_dependency_boundary.py` owns `HOSTED_TELEMETRY_DISTRIBUTIONS` and its three assertions (declared, imported, resolvable); this module imports that table and adds only the package-import assertion inside the combined framework test, so the tracing row of the technology table has a test it can point at without a second copy of the list.

A blocklist is not exhaustive and is not claimed to be. A vector store nobody has heard of is not in `SECOND_STORE_DISTRIBUTIONS`; what actually closes the set is `tests/test_dependency_boundary.py`'s equality against the four approved distributions, which is exhaustive by construction. The tables here are the second line and their value is the error message — they say which rule is being broken and where the argument is. The decision record says this in 'What is claimed'.

No `guardrails` pytest marker and no `make guardrails`. The `conformance` marker exists because 'do the guarantees still hold' is a question an operator asks directly; these 11 tests are 28 s and answer nothing that `make check` does not already, so a second thing to remember to run would have been cost without a question behind it. Argued in the record's 'Alternatives rejected'.
lessons: A dependency boundary is not a store boundary, and the difference is the standard library. `tests/test_dependency_boundary.py` allows every name in `sys.stdlib_module_names` — it has to, the package is mostly standard library — so `import sqlite3`, `import shelve` and `import dbm` passed it by construction. The single-store invariant in concept/instruction.md §2 forbids 'no second database, no vector store, no checkpoint store, no file-backed agent memory', and not one of those four requires an install. Any future 'we have a test for that' about a store should be checked against whether the store needs a dependency at all.

The persistence target that no import scan can see is the one defined in SQL. `CREATE SINK ... WITH (connector = 'kafka', ...)` is a second egress channel with its own credentials, `CREATE SOURCE` with an S3 or Iceberg connector is a second store, and `CREATE SECRET` is a credential outside the environment. RisingWave exposes all four in `rw_catalog.rw_sources` / `rw_sinks` / `rw_connections` / `rw_secrets`, each carrying `schema_id`, so the query scopes cleanly to the migrated schema via `rw_catalog.rw_schemas`. Note that `rw_schemas` has columns (id, name, owner, acl) only — `current_schema()` cannot be joined in a subquery against it the way information_schema allows, so resolve the id in Python and parameterize.

Scope a source scan by what the name can also mean, or it gets widened until it checks nothing. The filesystem-write scan names six methods — write_text, write_bytes, touch, mkdir, makedirs, symlink_to — and deliberately not `write`, `remove`, `rename` or `replace`: helena.observability writes a log line to a TextIO and `str.replace` / `dataclasses.replace` are used throughout, so a scan for those fires on code that is not about files. `open()` is judged by its mode instead of its presence, with an unreadable mode treated as a write. This is task 49's ast-not-regex lesson one level down: the false positive is not prose here, it is a method name with a second meaning.

`uv run` installs what `pyproject.toml` declares, whether or not you asked it to. Editing the dependency list to induce a test failure put langgraph, langchain-core, langgraph-checkpoint, redis and about twenty transitive packages into `.venv/` — the very SDKs three tests exist to keep out. `uv.lock` was NOT modified (git status confirmed) and `uv sync` restored the environment exactly, but the window between the two is a suite that could have gone green or red for the wrong reason. Revert the file and run `uv sync` in the same command as the mutation, and check `ls .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages` rather than trusting the revert.

A meta-test over a concept note must fail in both directions or it only enforces half the rule. `test_the_technology_table_still_records_each_rejection` catches a row reworded or reversed; `test_every_rejection_in_the_technology_table_has_a_test_here` catches a row added with nothing carrying it. Neither forbids the note from changing — concept/ is the authority — what they forbid is the note changing without the decision record and the test landing in the same commit.
failed_approaches: task 50: Inducing a 'rejected dependency is declared' failure by editing pyproject.toml and running `uv run pytest`. It works — both tests go red with the right message — but `uv run` syncs the environment first, so it also INSTALLS the rejected packages. langgraph, langchain-core, langgraph-checkpoint, langgraph-sdk, redis and their transitive set landed in `.venv/`, which is precisely what `test_no_second_store_client_is_declared_imported_or_installed` and the hosted-telemetry tests exist to prevent. `uv.lock` was untouched and `uv sync` cleaned it up completely, but do the mutation, the revert and `uv sync` as one command, and verify with `ls .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages` before running anything that asserts on the environment.

task 50: Backgrounding the full suite with `nohup uv run pytest -q > log 2>&1 &` inside a Bash call that also had `run_in_background: true`. The tracked command is then the shell that backgrounds it, which exits in milliseconds, so the completion notification arrives immediately and says exit 0 while the suite has barely started collecting. The log tail at that moment was 44 bytes of dots and looked like a truncated pass. Use one or the other: either `run_in_background` on the pytest command itself, or a foreground `until ! pgrep -x pytest; do sleep N; done` waiter.

task 50: A first draft of `_rejected(table, kind)` took a `kind` string used by nothing but an `assert kind` to silence the unused argument. That is the one-value config key concept/instruction.md §1 says to inline; it was removed and the call sites simplified before the final suite run.

task 50: Editing the test module while a full suite run was in flight. Caught before it mattered — the run was stopped with `pkill -x pytest` (never `-f`, see task 49) and restarted against the final tree — but it is the same trap task 49 recorded: a run that has already collected a file validates a version of it that no longer exists.
next_session_should_know: The five architectural rejections are tests now, and the gate is proved rather than asserted. SIX THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THERE ARE NOW THREE BOUNDARY MODULES AND THEY OWN DIFFERENT THINGS. `tests/test_dependency_boundary.py` owns THE APPROVED SET — the equality against four distributions, the package's imports, and hosted telemetry declared/imported/installed. `tests/test_broker.py` owns THE BROKER RULE INSIDE `helena/broker.py` — one client, eight wire-protocol names, no other network module, no address literal. `tests/test_architecture_boundary.py` owns THE FIVE REJECTIONS IN `concept/06-technology.md` and the gaps neither reached. They import each other's helpers rather than restating them: the new module imports `_declared`, `_package_modules`, `_pyproject`, `_top_level_imports`, `APPROVED_RUNTIME_DISTRIBUTIONS` and `HOSTED_TELEMETRY_DISTRIBUTIONS` from the dependency module. If you extend one, check the other two do not already hold it — a second definition of one property is worse than none. (2) ADDING A REJECTION ROW TO `concept/06-technology.md` MEANS ADDING A TEST, AND REVERSING ONE MEANS A DECISION RECORD. Both are enforced: `REJECTIONS` holds each Concern and its Choice cell verbatim, `_technology_table()` re-parses the note every run, and `test_reversing_a_rejection_requires_a_decision_record` requires `docs/decisions/0039-architectural-boundaries.md` to exist AND to name every rejection. All four failure modes were induced and reverted. A row whose Choice is 'Not adopted', 'Rejected' or 'Deferred' and is not in `REJECTIONS` is red. (3) THE PACKAGE WRITES NO FILE AND STARTS NO PROCESS, AND THAT IS NOW A TEST. If an increment needs to write a path — a cache, a checkpoint, a scratch file, a subprocess to a CLI — it will fail `test_the_package_writes_to_no_file_and_starts_no_process`, and that failure is the escalation, not an obstacle to route around. Reads are unchecked and always fine. The scan names six unambiguous write methods and judges `open()` by its mode; do not widen it to `write`, `remove`, `rename` or `replace`, which have other meanings in this package and would make it fire on `helena.observability` and on `str.replace`. (4) THE ENGINE'S CATALOGUE IS PART OF THE BOUNDARY NOW. `test_the_migrated_schema_defines_no_source_sink_connection_or_secret` requires `rw_sources`, `rw_sinks`, `rw_connections` and `rw_secrets` to be empty for the migrated schema. A migration adding `CREATE SINK ... WITH (connector = ...)` is red — which is correct, because `sql/migrations/0019_sink.sql` already recorded WHY emission is a plain view read by deterministic code over the Kafka wire protocol rather than a `CREATE SINK`: the enriched context derives `status` from `now()`, and a streaming query rejects that. (5) NEVER MUTATE `pyproject.toml` TO TEST A DEPENDENCY GUARD WITHOUT `uv sync` IN THE SAME COMMAND. `uv run` syncs before it runs, so declaring a package installs it — this session briefly had langgraph, langchain-core, langgraph-checkpoint and redis in `.venv/`. `uv.lock` was not touched and `uv sync` restored it, but verify with `ls .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages` rather than trusting the revert. (6) A DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE IS STILL OPEN AND THIS MODULE DOES NOT TOUCH IT. `concept/06-technology.md` lists LangChain as the ADOPTED model client, and this repository does not use it — `helena.agents` reaches the OpenAI-compatible endpoint with `urllib`, because `langchain-openai` resolves to 37 distributions including `langsmith`, and the hosted-tracing rule is 'not at all' rather than 'not yet'. That is task 30's escalation, recorded in `docs/decisions/0020-the-model-client.md` §1, and it is still open. The meta-tests here cover only the REFUSAL rows of the table, so they neither enforce nor contradict that row; it returns with the analyst's tool loop.
